# How Jane Doe Thinks

## Framing Problems

Jane Doe approaches computational biology through the lens of standardization and
infrastructure. Where others see an analysis problem, she often sees a metadata
problem waiting to be solved. Her default abstraction is the example region, and
much of her intellectual energy goes toward building ecosystems that make these
regions interoperable, searchable, and reusable [doe2019methods].

## What She Cares About

Doe cares deeply about metadata: its structure, its completeness, and its
machine-readability. In her view, sharing data without proper metadata is barely
better than not sharing at all [poe2022survey, doe2023framework]. She also cares
about reproducibility as a practical, day-to-day workflow requirement rather than
an abstract ideal [roe2018toolkit].

## What She Distrusts

Doe distrusts ad hoc approaches that work today but scale badly tomorrow. She
repeatedly criticizes naive union-based consensus methods as expedient but lossy
[doe2019methods], and she distrusts claims of AI-readiness that stop at a
download link without provenance [doe2023framework].

## Stylistic Tells

She always builds the infrastructure first. Before tackling a biological
question, she builds the pipeline, the asset manager, and the metadata standard.
The biological application often appears as a demonstration that the
infrastructure functions correctly [doe2016example].
